subject: How to implement a function that adds attributes to html tag?

messages.author: a1bf76ab9a5a2d4b
messages.subject: How to implement a function that adds attributes to html tag?
parts:
Hey Shiny users,

I'm looking for a simple and clean solution to the following problem (I don't think it's supposed to be very hard..)

Let's say I want to create a function that takes an HTML tag and simply adds a class "testclass" to it.  If there is already a class on it, then it should add another class, and otherwise it should create a "class" attribute with "testclass".

For example:
addTestClass(div("mydiv"))    ==>  "<div class="testclass">mydiv</div>
addTestClass(div(id = "myid", class = "someclass", "mydiv"))    ==>  "<div id="myid" class="someclass testclass">mydiv</div>

(I want a function more complex than that, but having this simple case would make it very easy to generalize)

Let me know if you have a nice approach, for some reason I can't think of a very nice implementation. Thanks!

messages.author: 55771919c42cb6a1
messages.subject: Re: How to implement a function that adds attributes to html tag?
parts:
This should do the trick:

addTestClass <- function(tag) {
  # Use paste() with collapse so that there's no leading space when existing
  # class is NULL.
  tag$attribs$class <- paste(c(tag$attribs$class, "someclass"), collapse = " ")
  tag
}


x <- div("mydiv")
y <- div("mydiv", class = "one")
z <- div("mydiv", class = "one two")


addTestClass(x)
# <div class="someclass">mydiv</div> 

addTestClass(y)
# <div class="one someclass">mydiv</div> 

addTestClass(z)
# <div class="one two someclass">mydiv</div> 


-Winston

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: How to implement a function that adds attributes to html tag?
parts:
That's actually not right--don't manipulate the tag list directly, instead use htmltools::tagAppendAttributes(). It's smart enough to combine duplicate attributes.

> library(htmltools)
> library(magrittr)
> tags$div(class = "foo") %>% tagAppendAttributes(class = "bar")
<div class="foo bar"></div>
On Mon, Jan 26, 2015 at 9:19 PM, Dean Attali <daat...@gmail.com> wrote:

That is exactly what I wanted, I did not know about the tag$attribs.  Should have figured it out by looking at a tag's structure.... thanks!
